title: no-halt-agent Sprint 2: pipe モード + claude-agent ロスレス生存 [MILESTONE]

planning_decisions.decision: Story granularity kept as-is (3 stories, no split).
planning_decisions.rationale: The three stories are cleanly layered and non-overlapping in BEHAVIOR: (1) spike = measure real-claude control_request deadline (gating), (2) mechanism = pipe-mode ptyhost + generic offset-ack line replay + persistence + overflow detection (fake-emitter verifiable, no claude), (3) adoption = claudeagent.Client thin-client + permstate/transcript reconstruction + real-claude E2E. No story bundles independent behaviors that warrant a split. The task's suggested breakdown matches the natural mechanism-vs-consumer seam.

Story 1 is a gating spike whose result can trigger an ADR-0004 revisit — it MUST complete and PASS before any mechanism is built. Story 2 and Story 3 both extend the pipe-mode ptyhost AND share internal/tab/claudeagent files (Story 2 lands the generic replay client + offset store there; Story 3 rewrites client.go/manager.go + adds discover.go in the same package). Overlapping file-touch + the mechanism→consumer dependency make parallelism unsafe.

planning_decisions.decision: Reuse the S3f2658 ptyhost wire almost entirely; the ONLY sanctioned protocol growth is a stderr-delivery frame (or 1-byte stream discriminator) for pipe mode.
planning_decisions.rationale: priority_rule 6 + ADR-0002 (frozen-minimal protocol). The Ring is already absolute-offset; MsgAck/MsgAttach/MsgData/MsgStatus already exist and Ring.readFromLocked already returns the clamped start offset (which IS the overflow-detection primitive). So pipe mode needs only: mode-aware spawn (pipes vs PTY), a stdin-write path (reuse MsgInput), a no-op resize, and a way to deliver stderr separately from the NDJSON stdout stream. Adding one stderr frame is mandated by the design doc §6 ('stderr は別チャネル') and justified by ADR-0004, so it is not an ADR-0002 violation — but the implementer must keep it to the single minimal addition and record the exact wire choice in the run-phase decisions.

planning_decisions.decision: Overflow detection is palmux2-side via the clamped ATTACH start offset; ptyhost does NOT persist and does NOT auto-deny pending requests.
planning_decisions.rationale: ADR-0002 thin-holder + ADR-0004. The ptyhost holds the ring and echoes the clamped start offset it already computes; palmux2 compares requested-last-ack vs returned-start and, if start > requested, declares 'lossless restore impossible → new session'. Persistence (sessions.json-equivalent last-ack) lives in palmux2 (Story 2 store). This keeps the surviving old-binary ptyhost claude-agnostic and the socket protocol frozen.

planning_decisions.decision: Replay reconstruction of transcript + permstate reuses the UNCHANGED processStreamMessage path — replayed NDJSON lines are fed back through the same parser.
planning_decisions.rationale: ADR-0004's core premise is that the stdout stream is the source of truth for transcript/permstate/MCP state. Therefore replaying last-ack+ lines through the existing normalize.go/permstate.go/transcript.go rebuilds state for free. normalize/permstate/transcript/mcp stay palmux2-side and unchanged (ADR-0002/0004), minimizing regression surface for AC-3-3.

planning_decisions.decision: The incus (in-container) agent path becomes an OPAQUE argv handed to a pipe-mode ptyhost, exactly as claudetui.spawnWithArgs does for the PTY path.
planning_decisions.rationale: Today claudeagent uses runtime.ExecCommander (incus exec, no -t, binary-clean) which returns an *exec.Cmd. For ptyhost the child must be an opaque argv/env/cwd. Convert via argv=[cmd.Path, cmd.Args[1:]...], env=cmd.Env, cwd=cmd.Dir — the identical technique S3f2658 used for the PTYCommander wrapper. ExecCommander's no-TTY binary-clean property is exactly what pipe mode needs.

spike.question: Does the claude CLI wait for (and accept) a response to an MCP-routed permission control_request LONGER than palmux2's realistic restart window (a few seconds to ~15s)? Or does it time out / cancel / abort the tool first?
spike.method: Go spike harness reusing claudeagent transport primitives (mirror ask_integration_test.go / bash_perm_integration_test.go real-claude wiring): spawn real claude in stream-json mode with an in-process MCP permission server, force a permission control_request, WITHHOLD the response for tiered delays (10s/30s/60s), then send allow and record whether the late response is accepted + the tool executes + the turn continues.
spike.gate: ADR-0004 revisit + HALT (escalate to user) IF the late allow is NOT accepted at ~15s (deadline shorter than restart window). PASS ⇒ proceed to Wave 2.

waves.rationale: Gating spike — REAL claude control_request deadline. Must PASS before building the replay mechanism it validates; a FAIL triggers an ADR-0004 revisit and halts the sprint (priority_rule 0).

Pipe-mode ptyhost + generic line-oriented offset-ack replay + persistence store + ring-overflow detection. Fully verifiable with a fake NDJSON emitter (no claude, no quota). Depends on the Wave-1 spike PASS.

claudeagent.Client thin-client migration onto the Wave-2 mechanism + permstate/transcript replay reconstruction + real-claude restart-crossing E2E. Depends on Wave 2 (mechanism) and shares claudeagent files with it, so it runs strictly after.

new_test_or_harness: internal/tab/claudeagent/spike_control_deadline_test.go (env-gated real-claude spike harness, mirroring ask_integration_test.go / bash_perm_integration_test.go) OR an equivalent throwaway harness under tests/
S862203-1.note: Pure spike — NO production code changes. Reuses existing claudeagent transport + MCP primitives at the library level to observe the exact production wire path.

internal/ptyhost/ring.go (reuse as-is; instantiate a SECOND ring for stderr — likely no Ring code change)

internal/tab/claudeagent/ptyclient.go (NEW — generic line-oriented pipe-replay client: dial/HELLO/ATTACH-from-last-ack, NDJSON line reassembly across DATA boundaries, ACK-at-line-end, overflow detection)
internal/tab/claudeagent/offsetstore.go (NEW — sessions.json-equivalent last-ack offset persistence, atomic write; may extend existing store.go/sessions.go instead)
new_test: internal/ptyhost/pipe_test.go / server_test.go additions (pipe-mode spawn, stdout/stderr separation, kill-9 restart, overflow) with a FAKE NDJSON emitter child (testdata helper)
S862203-2.note: Touches internal/ptyhost AND internal/tab/claudeagent (the generic replay client + offset store land where Story 3 consumes them). This shared-package touch with Story 3 is the reason the two waves are serial.

production: internal/tab/claudeagent/client.go (LARGE — replace exec+StdinPipe/StdoutPipe/StderrPipe with pipe-mode ptyhost launch/attach; pumpStdout→Story-2 line replay client; pumpStderr→separate stderr channel; writeLine→INPUT frames; Close→SHUTDOWN/GC. Keep ALL argv/env assembly + control/MCP handling)

internal/tab/claudeagent/manager.go (EnsureClient launches via ptyhost; watchClient exit-detection via socket STATUS/disconnect; respawn = new pipe-mode ptyhost; --resume/invalid-resume/gate logic preserved)

internal/tab/claudeagent/discover.go (NEW — reconnect surviving agent ptyhosts on palmux2 startup + replay-driven permstate/transcript/pending-request reconstruction; mirror internal/tab/claudetui/discover.go DiscoverAndRestore)

cmd/palmux/main.go (invoke agent DiscoverAndRestore on startup, mirror the claudetui wiring)

S862203-3.note: Highest-risk migration. Shares client.go/manager.go/store with Story 2 → serial.

real_claude_requirements.S862203-1: REQUIRED — the AC's whole purpose is real-claude control_request deadline behavior. Fake emitter cannot answer it. Runs on this box's real `claude`. Gates the sprint.
real_claude_requirements.S862203-2: NOT needed — fake NDJSON emitter (counter-tagged lines, controllable pace) as the ptyhost child makes ring/ACK/offset/replay/overflow + kill-9 restart deterministic and quota-free.
real_claude_requirements.S862203-3: AC-3-2 REQUIRED — real claude on `make serve INSTANCE=dev` (NEVER host palmux2): restart palmux2 mid-turn, prove (a) lossless transcript restore and (b) a restart-window permission request delivered→answered→tool executes. AC-3-1 wiring: fake emitter OK. AC-3-3: existing claudeagent unit + real-claude integration suite (ask/bash_perm/plan) regress cleanly.

forbidden_reminders: Do NOT restart/foreground the host palmux2 (it would kill the operator's live Claude session). All E2E/survival runs use `make serve INSTANCE=dev` (separate portman name + --tmux-prefix _pmx_dev_).
Ports via portman only; tmux via internal/tmux.Client only; no ~/.claude writes.

priority_rule 0: NEVER mark AC-S862203-1-1 or AC-S862203-3-2 as skipped/false-done. If a real-claude run is truly impossible under autopilot, escalate at the milestone review — do not fabricate a PASS.
adr_gate: If S862203-1 FAILS (claude aborts the control_request before ~15s), STOP: escalate an ADR-0004 revisit to the user (options per ADR notes: rely on claude to re-send the pending request on reconnect, or have ptyhost hold the request without auto-deny). Waves 2-3 assume the spike PASS.
